paper, template, coloring tools, scissors, glue

A resist lesson where marine invertebrates are drawn in permanent marker, colored with oil pastels or crayons, and the background painted in watercolor. Grade-by-grade standards are listed, helpful for lesson planning.
oil pastels or crayons, watercolor paint, brush, paper, permanent marker
A resist short where jellyfish are drawn in crayon and washed with watercolor for an undersea feel. It is brief with a colorful result, good to show at the start of a lesson.

An art lesson introducing the agamograph, a kinetic art form that holds two pictures in one, and making one together. The teacher addresses students directly, so it can be shown in class as is.

A video presenting ten printmaking activities with simple materials, such as homemade stamps, monoprints, toy printing, bubble prints, shaving-foam marbling, chalk and tissue prints, and nature prints. The creator's blog has a post for each, so you can pick one to suit your grade and supplies.
paint, paper, printing materials for each idea (stamps, toys, chalk, tissue paper, shaving foam, natural objects)
An elementary art teacher shows the process of making a Roman-style mosaic with colored paper. It lets you combine ancient Rome studies with art.

A video painting two scenes in acrylic, cutting them into strips and mounting them accordion-style so the image changes with viewing angle. Materials and colors are listed in the description for easy prep.
acrylic paint, white cartridge paper, round brush, paper cutter, ruler, glue stick

A Valentine-themed short painting a jar of hearts using wax resist and watercolor. Brief with a cute result, it suits seasonal event art.
watercolor paint, brush, paper, wax (candle or white crayon)
A tie-dye T-shirt short where fabric is bound, wetted and dyed with diluted dye to form patterns. The description briefly explains how bound areas resist the dye.
white T-shirt, dye, rubber bands, spray bottle, plastic tray

A marbling short where shaving foam is spread on a tray, paint is dropped and swirled with a stick, and paper is pressed on to take a print. Materials and steps are listed in the description, making prep easy.
shaving foam, tempera paint, thick paper or cardstock, popsicle stick or skewer, squeegee or straight edge
A short video showing step by step how to accordion-fold an agamograph. It is a handy support clip for students who get stuck at the folding stage after drawing.
Three-Piece Agamograph Part 4: Making the Base
Part 4 of a series on an agamograph showing three changing pictures, focusing on making the stand. Use it as the finishing step together with the earlier parts of the series.
A one-minute video making an agamograph of a cartoon character that changes with viewing angle. Using a character students know helps grab their interest.
A ten-minute video showing how to make a mosaic piece in a way children can follow. It suggests giving the finished work as a gift to parents or friends.

A preschool–lower grade lesson making a name mosaic by gluing warm- or cool-colored paper strip pieces over a name written on black paper. It also suggests making color patterns for students who finish easily.
paper strips sorted into warm and cool colors, black paper with names written, scissors, glue stick
A museum education video showing how to make an agamograph whose image changes with viewing angle. In under three minutes, it covers the key process.
A grade 5 lesson inspired by Yaacov Agam, making an agamograph where emoji pictures swap. It requires precise work with ruler, glue and scissors, suiting an upper-grade challenge.
A short on making marbled paper with kids. There is no description, so check materials in the video, but it works as a quick opener showing marbled results.
Day and Night Agamograph Step by Step
A video that explains what an agamograph is and who created it, then makes a day-and-night illusion piece step by step. It covers both appreciation and making in one video.
Shape Art with Chalk and Stencils
A lower-grade art lesson where chalk is applied around stencils and smudged outward to show various shapes. It is presented as an activity for learning shapes and building fine motor skills.
An art teacher's lesson of about eight minutes on how to make an agamograph. There is no description, but its classroom format makes it easy to follow together in class.
An art activity video using the hand as a stencil for a drawing. The description is only the title, so check materials in the video, but using one's own hand makes it easy for anyone to start.
Crayon and Watercolor Resist Under the Sea
A resist video where sea creatures are drawn in crayon and washed with watercolor to complete an undersea scene. At five minutes, it shows the whole process at a glance.

A short where a calligrapher deliberately shows four things you should not do while writing with a brush and invites viewers to spot them. It works as a quiz-style opener on posture and habits before a calligraphy lesson.
